verdict.line: You lose if you get parried into a bad trade or dove before level 6; you win if you survive that window and let your mid-game item spikes take over.

brief.thesis: Fiora holds lane and solo-kill advantage because Riposte (W) punishes any raw engage and the double-dash on Lunge (Q) lets her poke and disengage before you can answer, which is why the matchup grades as defensive despite Camille sitting at a 52% record over 171 games. Camille's actual leverage is sequencing: land W (Tactical Sweep) for its cone poke, slow, and heal before you ever throw E (Hookshot), and hold the Q (Precision Protocol) recast for the delayed, bigger hit instead of spending it on reflex. Once Trinity Force and Ravenous Hydra are online, short forced trades stop favoring her Duelist passive healing and the lane evens out.

theirWindow.what: Any auto-attack or E (Hookshot) follow-up you throw into this gets parried, boosting her AD and reflecting magic damage back at you. Hold your engage and just farm or poke with W (Tactical Sweep) from range instead.

yourWindow.what: This is your window to commit E (Hookshot, cooldown 16/15/14/13/12s) off a nearby wall for the knock-up, then follow with Q (Precision Protocol) and let the recast ride for the bigger delayed hit.

powerCurve.note: Lunge (Q) poke outranges your trade tools
Riposte punishes engages, Burst of Speed threatens kills
Hextech Ultimatum gives you a real pick tool
Trinity Force plus Hydra flips short trades
Death's Dance and Sterak's blunt her all-in

start.why: Highest measured win rate start in this matchup (54.3% over 127 games, 63.8% pick) — the extra AD and sustain from autos help you survive Fiora's Lunge poke without a recall.

boots.why: 53.8% win rate over 145 games and 86.3% pick rate — Fiora's damage is entirely auto-attack and Lunge-based, so flat physical reduction directly cuts her trading and all-in damage.

core.why: First item in the highest win rate path (62.1% over 29 games) — the damage and move speed spike is what lets you start winning short trades instead of just surviving them.
Second in the same 62.1% path — sustain and cleave help you shove waves fast enough to punish her Duelist stacking with tempo.
Final item in the 39.2%-picked, 62.1% win rate path — the damage-over-time conversion directly softens Blade Waltz burst once she's level 6.

situational.when: she is stacking Duelist heals every trade and you can't out-damage the regen
you are ahead and need to survive a Blade Waltz all-in instead of just outtrading her
you are snowballing and want lower cooldowns on Q and E for extended skirmishes

runes.keystoneWhy: Best measured page in this matchup (52.5% win rate, 20.2% pick) — the bonus health and proc heal on autos directly counter a lane where you're behind on kill pressure and need to win the war of attrition, not the burst trade.

summoners.why: Most picked combo (71.1% pick, 52.1% win rate) — Ignite offsets Fiora's Duelist healing in an all-in and Flash lets you land Hookshot (E) engages or escape her Lunge chain. If you expect to lose the early trades outright, Teleport plus Ignite has the highest measured win rate in this matchup (61% over fewer games) by letting you skip the losing exchanges and reset on wave.

playing.title: Don't autoattack into Riposte
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this matchup is to avoid walking into Riposte (W, cooldown 10/9/8/7/6s) by not using your second Hookshot engage the instant it's up. Wait for her parry to be confirmed down before committing autos.

playing.title: Delay your Q recast for burst
playing.detail: Precision Protocol's recast deals significantly more damage the longer you wait between the two hits. Save the delayed recast for your actual all-in instead of firing it off on the first empowered auto.

playing.title: Poke with W before you commit E
playing.detail: Tactical Sweep (cooldown 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, range 610) is a delayed cone that slows and does bonus damage in its outer half while healing you. Land it first so you're already ahead on the health trade before you dive in.

playing.title: Only throw E on a landed knock-up
playing.detail: Hookshot (cooldown 16/15/14/13/12s, range 800) requires a wall and only knocks up on landing. Don't burn it chasing during her Burst of Speed (E, cooldown 15/14/13/12/11s) — she'll simply outrun it.

playing.title: Expect the second Lunge
playing.detail: Fiora's Q can dash a second time within a couple seconds at no mana cost. Dodging the first hit doesn't end the trade — disengage instead of trading through the follow-up.

playing.title: Time R around her Riposte, not before it
playing.detail: The Hextech Ultimatum (cooldown 140/115/90/0/0s, range 475) anchors her in your zone, but if Riposte is still up she parries your first landing auto and denies the bonus magic damage. Confirm her W is down before committing R.

playing.title: Respect Blade Waltz once she hits 6
playing.detail: Blade Waltz (cooldown 130/120/110/110/110s, range 400) dashes to hit her successively with diminishing returns per hit but closes distance fast. Don't sit at low health after a trade — it's a kill tool, not just a duel finisher.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win rate/pick rate figures are measured from real games on the current patch via OP.GG; the sequencing, timing, and trade-pattern reasoning are this brief's own tactical read, not OP.GG's.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of being hit with Fiora’s Vitals (P) often! Try to avoid being hit with Riposte (W) by not using the second Hookshot [E] immediately. Aim for when Riposte (W) is on cooldown!
